JAZZ ON THE LAWN AT FULHAM PALACE


Welcome to the online home of Jazz on the Lawn at Fulham Palace. With two brilliant nights of music presented on the lawns of this charming historic property first established in AD 704, it's a delightful way to spend a summer evening.

THE SHOW GOES ON RAIN OR SHINE

Fulham Palace Map, Transport & Parking page
 

ONLINE SALES HAVE NOW ENDED, BUT TICKETS WILL BE SOLD ON THE DOOR

Friday 17 July, 2026
Doors 6:30pm :: Show 7:30pm :: Show Ends 10pm

THE COALMINERS

GENERAL ADMISSION
Adults/Youth 11 & Up: £25.00 :: Children 4-10: £14 :: Children 3 & under: Free*

With their dedication to what they to refer to as “Swamp Soul” this brilliant band, with their unique mixture of New Orleans Groove and Funk, bring the rhythm and soul of the deep south (that's Louisiana, not Brighton...) alive. And if you are used to seeing them at the 606 Club be prepared to be bowled over with the addition of a 3-piece horn section, making this one of the most powerful and charismatic 10-piece bands in the UK. Featuring vocalists Tommy Hare & Amy Bird this highly impressive line-up are guaranteed to raise the roof!  VIEW VIDEO CLIP

"Riotous uplifting funk bursting at the seams, plus raw powerful vocals. Get down to the Coalminers immediately!" Jazz FM 

Tickets may be returned up until 48 hours before the event, after which no cash returns will be available. Tickets may be exchanged for 606 vouchers on a case-by-case basis at the discretion of the club. Please read our Terms and Conditions in full below. 

ONLINE TICKET SALES HAVE NOW ENDED. 
HOWEVER, THERE ARE PLENTY OF TICKETS AVAILABLE ON THE DOOR FROM 6:30PM. SEE YOU THERE! Questions? Call the office 020 7352 5953 & we'll be glad to assist. 

Saturday 18 July, 2026
Doors 6:30pm :: Show 7:30pm :: Show Ends 10pm

606 CLUB ALL STARS 50TH ANNIVERSARY CELEBRATION

GENERAL ADMISSION
Adults/Youth 11 & Up: £25.00 :: Children 4-10: £14 :: Children 3 & under: Free*

Tonight, previewing the 606 Club’s 50th Anniversary, we are bringing to Fulham Palace for the first time our amazing “606 All Stars” 9 piece band. Featuring three world class vocalists, three Internationally recognised horn players and a rhythm section to die for, this promises to be a phenomenal night of jazz to remember. Singers featured this evening will be Natalie Duncan, Polly Gibbons & Jo Harrop alongside 606 Club stalwarts, saxophonists Brandon Allen, Alec Harper & Denys Baptiste. VIEW VIDEO CLIP

“[Duncan] She draws comparisons with Nina Simone and Alicia Keys…a voice whose honeyed, silky caresses are to die for” MOJO;  “[Harrop] A singing sensation… her voice is amazing…a class act”  BeBop Spoken Here; “[Gibbons] truly exceptional…possessing a voice of such sizzling intensity and raw emotion you could fry an egg on it” Jazzwise

Tickets may be returned up until 48 hours before the event, after which no cash returns will be available. Tickets may be exchanged for 606 vouchers on a case-by-case basis at the discretion of the club. Please read our Terms and Conditions in full below. 

ONLINE TICKET SALES HAVE NOW ENDED. 
HOWEVER, THERE ARE PLENTY OF TICKETS AVAILABLE ON THE DOOR FROM 6:30PM. SEE YOU THERE! Questions? Call the office 020 7352 5953 & we'll be glad to assist. 

General Information

WEATHER: The show goes on rain or shine. 

FOOD AND DRINK: The Club will be hosting a full bar serving beer, wine, champagne & spirits, including pours from our latest sponsor, Emissary who will be pouring "Exceptional Cuvées - Prosecco, Crémant & Beyond". 

We'll also have food available for purchase from Fulham Palace's own Cafe, including meat, vegetarian and vegan options such as a proper Cornish Sausage roll, Cheese and tomato calzone pizzini, fresh sandwiches and crisps, popcorn and nuts. 

However guests are absolutely welcome to bring their own picnics to enjoy, as well as beverages including alcohol.

SEATING: This event takes place on the main lawn of Fulham Palace. Chairs and tables are not provided with your ticket though are available to rent in advance for a small fee (we cannot guarantee availability of tables on the night itself unless they are pre-booked). You may also bring your own blanket or low-backed chair if you wish, but Fulham Palace stipulates that they "not damage the Lawn as it is an area of archaeological significance. Therefore, furniture must not dig into the ground, as this could risk damaging the historic site." 
UPDATE: All tables are currently pre-booked. However there are sometimes one or two cancellations on the day, which will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. We still have plenty of chairs. 

DISABLED ACCESS: Fulham Palace is quite easy to access; the grounds are level and there is a mix of grass with paved and unpaved paths. For more information, visit the Fulham Palace site. 

ANIMALS: With the exception of guide dogs, animals are not permitted at Fulham Palace.

PARKING & TRANSPORT:  There are many convenient ways to get to Fulham Palace, and street parking on Bishop's Avenue is generally available during the event (unless it's a Fulham FC match day). For detailed instructions, please visit the Fulham Palace Map, Transport & Parking page.

ON SITE SECURITY: For the safety and security of all present, we will be checking the bags of anyone attending the event prior to entry. After passing through security, customers will be provided with a colour-coded wristband to allow them to leave and re-enter the Palace grounds if they wish. Security provided by http://rocknrollsecurity.com/.

*Children are very welcome to attend however must be supervised throughout by an adult, and consideration must be given not to disturb other audience members enjoying the performance.

TERMS AND CONDITIONS: Tickets may be returned up until 48 hours before the event, after which no cash returns will be available. Tickets may be exchanged for 606 vouchers on a case-by-case basis at the discretion of the club. In the event of another Covid-related lockdown forcing us to cancel the event, we will issue refunds for all purchases made up to and until the cancellation date less 20% for fixed costs (costs to suppliers for which we are liable regardless of cancellation). We may also be required to implement specific Covid-related health and safety policies as directed by the Council or other government authority, but are unknown to us at this time. We will update our website as this information becomes available. For any questions regarding the above conditions please contact us at 'jazz@606club.co.uk".

Tommaso Starace Organ Trio - Album Launch

Wednesday 9th September 2026 - 8:00 pm

Music Charge: £18.00

Book Now

Italo-Australian saxophonist Tommaso Starace moved from Milan to the UK to study, first at Birmingham Conservatoire and later at the Guildhall School Of Music and Drama where he gained a postgraduate degree in jazz studies. He has performed at many of the top European jazz clubs and festivals, and has worked with some of the most respected jazz musicians including Billy Cobham, David Liebman, Kenny Wheeler and Stan Sulzmann. He's also collaborated with Oscar award-winning film composer Dario Marianelli ('Atonement' and 'Pride and Prejudice') recording music for 'This Little Life', a BBC drama for Channel Four. With 10 albums already to his name, tonight Tommaso is performing at the Club for the first time as a band leader to launch his latest organ trio album 'Live at the Beaver Inn'. Featuring Martin Jenkins-Hammond organ and Pip Harbon-drums, not only will the trio play tracks from the album but they'll also be exploring some of the more unusual jazz repertoire from composers such as Monk, Kenny Barron, Cedar Walton & Benny Golson. Expect an evening of hard swinging music fueled by lots of energy and adrenaline.

"Starace is on fire...An excellent album worthy of the vintage Blue Note or Prestige label" Lance Liddle (Bebop Spoken Here Blog);  “Anyone who has experienced a glissando of language on the streets of Italy will understand the utter exuberance with which Italian-born Starace attacks and runs with the language of music” Paul Medley, The Oxford Times; “This isn't the organ trio in funky club mode, more a vehicle for high-energy improvisation, tough-sounding and intent… it's the fleet post-Parkerian alto of Milan-born Starace, UK-based since 1994, that takes charge” Peter Vacher/Jazzwise

Photo by Ron Milsom

Andres Lafone's South Atlantic Groove Project (SAGP) ft. Joanna Eden

Tuesday 8th September 2026 - 8:00 pm

Music Charge: £18.00

Book Now

Andrés ‘Andy’ Lafone, Uruguayan bass player, co-founder and musical director of hit makers Negrocan introduces his new venture SAGP (South Atlantic Groove Project). Accompanied by fellow Uruguayans Guille Hill (guitar), Andres Ticino (percussion), plus award winning saxophonist Tony Kofi and Kevin Robinson (trumpet) with Joanna Eden on piano/vocals, they revisit tunes by Airto, Opa, Santana, Negrocan, and add some original compositions with a distinct groove-based South American flavour.

A very old friend of the Club, Andy moved to London in the late 70's and has been here ever since. A leading light of the Latin American music scene in the UK and Europe, he came to prominence in the late 80's and early 90's as part of the Jazz Dance/Acid Jazz movement and has, since then, toured and recorded worldwide with Basia (picking up a gold record along the way), New Orleans-based singer/pianist Jon Cleary, leading UK Latin musician/bandleader Snowboy and iconic Latin band Da Lata. With Negrocan, Andy’s composition ‘Cada Vez’ was nominated for a Billboard Award in 2002 as well as the “Song of the Summer’ award in Ibiza, becoming a worldwide hit!  Joanna Eden first established herself as a singer, pianist and songwriter to watch in the 2000’s and has nine solo albums to her credit, her latest album "The Road to Paysandu" was recorded in Uruguay with Andy, Hugo Fattoruso, and Albana Barrocas. Guille Hill is a first call guitarist for many Brazilian jazz bands and has worked with Mica Paris, Tom Jones and is a regular member of John Crawford's lineup. Tony Kofi is a multi-award winning saxophonist and with Lafone was a regular member of the Grand Union Orchestra. Kevin Robinson is well known as being a member of Simply Red since 2008, but has several other formidable credits as composer and conductor. A simply incredible lineup of musicians and not to be missed! 

"Andy Lafone....formidable talent" LatinosInLondon; “Eden…sings…sweetly and with conviction” Evening Standard

Elaine Delmar ft. Barry Green (Birthday Gig)

Sunday 13th September 2026 - 1:30 pm

Music Charge: £18.00

Book Now

It’s fair to say that after 60 years in the business Elaine Delmar is very much Jazz “Royalty”. From work at 16 with her father, the famous Leslie “Jiver” Hutchinson, through leading roles in stage musicals such as ‘Bubbling Brown Sugar’ in London and ‘Kern Goes to Hollywood’ on Broadway to a successful recording career that started in the 1960’s and continues to this day, Elaine has established herself as an international artist of talent, poise and grace. She has appeared in concert with the likes of Andy Williams, Michel Legrand and the London Symphony Orchestra (Royal Albert Hall) and it is a testament to the enormous respect with which she is held that in 2013 she received the APPJAG Special Parliamentary Jazz Award in recognition of her inestimable contribution to the UK jazz scene. Appearing this afternoon as a duo with the wonderful Barry Green-piano (Ian Shaw, Bobby Watson, Charles McPherson), Elaine will also be celebrating her birthday in style, performing music from her latest album "Speak Low" along with a programme of swinging standards. And watch out for her Special Birthday Guests!

"Truly defines the word class" BBC Radio 2; “The one who really shone was pianist Barry Green" Daily Telegraph

Jon Lloyd Quartet (Album Launch)

Thursday 17th September 2026 - 8:00 pm

Music Charge: £18.00

Book Now

Rising to prominence in the 1990’s as a saxophonist/composer of note associated with free jazz, Jon Lloyd and his quartet featuring renowned pianist John Law toured the UK and Europe prolifically, while working with Swiss label HatHut & the UK’s Leo Records. Over the years however his style has evolved towards a more European jazz aesthetic, while also incorporating touchpoints from American and contemporary jazz and even world music. The latest iteration of Jon’s quartet reunites him with John Law alongside bassist Nick Pini & drummer Alex Goodyear.  Tonight, following the success of their last album “Earth Songs” (also launched here at the Club), the quartet will be launching their latest album “Anima” to continue to promote their unique blend of European contemporary jazz. Featuring compositions by Jon he describes the music as “steeped in classic jazz, non-Western music, ECM melodic fusion and a hushed neo-classical grace”, creating a sound that is melodic, contemplative, and highly accessible to jazz and non-jazz audiences alike.  

“Ambitious and virtuosic. Jon Lloyd is one of the most striking writers at the sharp end of British jazz and improvisation” Guardian; “Lloyd’s tunes are steeped in the ECM aesthetic, and he and long-time collaborator John Law on piano make it sound like the only music you ever want to hear.” London Jazz News; “Creative music at its best. Great European contemporary jazz.” Jazzwise

Mo Pleasure Band

Sunday 30th August 2026 - 8:00 pm

Music Charge: £22.00

Book Now

One of the greatest multi-instrumentalists of his generation Morris "Mo" Pleasure has been at the forefront of American popular music for the last 30 years. A child prodigy, he began on piano at the age of 4 and by his early teens was also performing on bass, trumpet, guitar, drums and violin! After gaining a BA in Music in the mid 80's, Mo began his professional career playing with Ray Charles before moving in to the studios, including work with the likes of George Duke, Natalie Cole, Dianne Reeves, Christina Aguilera, Michael McDonald, Chaka Khan and Roberta Flack amongst many others. In 1993, he became a member of the legendary group Earth, Wind & Fire, ascending to become the band’s musical director from 1994-2001. He was featured with Janet Jackson, played keyboards and trumpet with Boney James and was recently MD for the iconic Bette Midler. Playing a mix of smooth jazz & groove material, Mo’s performances always have a great vibe. 

"...Pleasure proves that jazz can still be made which is smooth yet textured, is varied and interesting and can appeal to wide range of ears... Superb and essential." Soul Express

        <p id="breadcrumbs"><span><span><a href="https://londonirishcentre.org/">Home</a></span> » <span class="breadcrumb_last" aria-current="page">Run for Charity</span></span></p>        <h1><span>Run for Charity</span></h1>
        <h3></h3>
                                <p><strong>Whether it’s running a Half Marathon or the full 26.1 miles, taking on a challenge event for the London Irish Centre makes a real difference to the lives of those we support.  </strong></p>
<p><span data-contrast="auto">All the money you raise</span><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-contrast="auto">helps</span><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-contrast="auto">support</span><span data-contrast="auto"> our </span><span data-contrast="auto">c</span><span data-contrast="auto">harity’s</span><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-contrast="auto">vital </span><span data-contrast="auto">services</span><span data-contrast="auto">;</span><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-contrast="auto">alleviat</span><span data-contrast="auto">ing</span><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-contrast="auto">pov</span><span data-contrast="auto">erty</span><span data-contrast="auto">,</span><span data-contrast="auto"> </span><span data-contrast="auto">build</span><span data-contrast="auto">ing</span><span data-contrast="auto"> social </span><span data-contrast="auto">connection, and ensuring that </span><span data-contrast="auto">no </span><span data-contrast="auto">one </span><span data-contrast="auto">has to</span><span data-contrast="auto"> face </span><span data-contrast="auto">hardship a</span><span data-contrast="auto">lone.</span><span data-ccp-props="{}"> </span></p>

	jQuery(document).ready(function( $ ) {

// Select all links with hashes
$('a[href*="#"]')
  // Remove links that don't actually link to anything
  .not('[href="#"]')
  .not('[href="#0"]')
  .click(function(event) {
    // On-page links
    if (
      location.pathname.replace(/^\//, '') == this.pathname.replace(/^\//, '') 
      && 
      location.hostname == this.hostname
    ) {
      // Figure out element to scroll to
      var target = $(this.hash);
      target = target.length ? target : $('[name=' + this.hash.slice(1) + ']');
      // Does a scroll target exist?
      if (target.length) {
        // Only prevent default if animation is actually gonna happen
        event.preventDefault();
        $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 140
        }, 1000, function() {
          // Callback after animation
          // Must change focus!
          var $target = $(target);
          $target.focus();
          if ($target.is(":focus")) { // Checking if the target was focused
            return false;
          } else {
            $target.attr('tabindex','-1'); // Adding tabindex for elements not focusable
            $target.focus(); // Set focus again
          };
        });
      }
    }
  });

});

</script>

<script>
	jQuery(document).ready(function( $ ) {

// Select all links with hashes
$('a[href*="#"]')
  // Remove links that don't actually link to anything
  .not('[href="#"]')
  .not('[href="#0"]')
  .click(function(event) {
    // On-page links
    if (
      location.pathname.replace(/^\//, '') == this.pathname.replace(/^\//, '') 
      && 
      location.hostname == this.hostname
    ) {
      // Figure out element to scroll to
      var target = $(this.hash);
      target = target.length ? target : $('[name=' + this.hash.slice(1) + ']');
      // Does a scroll target exist?
      if (target.length) {
        // Only prevent default if animation is actually gonna happen
        event.preventDefault();
        $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 140
        }, 1000, function() {
          // Callback after animation
          // Must change focus!
          var $target = $(target);
          $target.focus();
          if ($target.is(":focus")) { // Checking if the target was focused
            return false;
          } else {
            $target.attr('tabindex','-1'); // Adding tabindex for elements not focusable
            $target.focus(); // Set focus again
          };
        });
      }
    }
  });

});

</script>

<script>
	jQuery(document).ready(function( $ ) {

// Select all links with hashes
$('a[href*="#"]')
  // Remove links that don't actually link to anything
  .not('[href="#"]')
  .not('[href="#0"]')
  .click(function(event) {
    // On-page links
    if (
      location.pathname.replace(/^\//, '') == this.pathname.replace(/^\//, '') 
      && 
      location.hostname == this.hostname
    ) {
      // Figure out element to scroll to
      var target = $(this.hash);
      target = target.length ? target : $('[name=' + this.hash.slice(1) + ']');
      // Does a scroll target exist?
      if (target.length) {
        // Only prevent default if animation is actually gonna happen
        event.preventDefault();
        $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 140
        }, 1000, function() {
          // Callback after animation
          // Must change focus!
          var $target = $(target);
          $target.focus();
          if ($target.is(":focus")) { // Checking if the target was focused
            return false;
          } else {
            $target.attr('tabindex','-1'); // Adding tabindex for elements not focusable
            $target.focus(); // Set focus again
          };
        });
      }
    }
  });

});

</script>

    if (
      location.pathname.replace(/^\//, '') == this.pathname.replace(/^\//, '') 
      && 
      location.hostname == this.hostname
    ) {
      // Figure out element to scroll to
      var target = $(this.hash);
      target = target.length ? target : $('[name=' + this.hash.slice(1) + ']');
      // Does a scroll target exist?
      if (target.length) {
        // Only prevent default if animation is actually gonna happen
        event.preventDefault();
        $('html, body').animate({
          scrollTop: target.offset().top - 140
        }, 1000, function() {
          // Callback after animation
          // Must change focus!
          var $target = $(target);
          $target.focus();
          if ($target.is(":focus")) { // Checking if the target was focused
            return false;
          } else {
            $target.attr('tabindex','-1'); // Adding tabindex for elements not focusable
            $target.focus(); // Set focus again
          };
        });
      }
    }
  });

});

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Formed in 2020 in Dearborn, Michigan, Prostitute is an experimental post-punk and Arab rock band. Born out of the isolation of the COVID-19 lockdown, the band’s debut album, Attempted Martyr, was written in the midst of global and personal turmoil, capturing the zeitgeist of a world unraveling. A loose concept record, it chronicles the rise and fall of a doomed zealot whose pursuit of holy vengeance spirals into a psychotic orgy of violence, greed, and lust.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The band was initially formed by Moe Kazra who enlisted childhood friends Andrew Kaster and Dylan Zaranski, with Ross Babinski and Bret Wall later completing the lineup. Together, they self-funded the album, working with legendary engineer Chris Koltay to shape a sound that's both abrasive and hypnotic—an unrelenting blend of warped guitars, primitive basslines, frenzied drumming, and corrosive synthesizers, interwoven with samples from diverse cultures, ranging from African to Middle Eastern and East Asian influences.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Tracks like “All Hail” (inspired by the 1977 Hanafi Siege of Washington D.C.) immerses listeners in a volatile, hostage-like environment. "Judge" channels Milton's Satan in a chilling rallying cry, while “Body Meat” grapples with religious desperation and the tenuous boundary between faith and madness. Khachab and Kaster’s lyrics have been described by Pitchfork as "disturbingly poetic" with the ability to "lacerate with image alone." Crude sloganeering and scenes of horrific violence are juxtaposed with literary allusion and Islamic symbolism, creating what the band calls a "theatricalization of terrorism." Through this lens, they examine and critique the xenophobic stereotypes targeted at Arabs, distorting them into grotesque caricatures.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Over the past four years, Prostitute has established a reputation for their punishing, high-energy performances. The band’s live shows, described as “dangerous” and “volatile”, finds Moe delivering politically charged sermons atop a deafening bacchanal of sound. In 2023, Prostitute performed at the re-opening of the iconic UFO Bar in Detroit, followed by a series of benefit concerts for Palestine, Lebanon, and Sudan. These performances solidified their growing presence, leading to invites to play at No Rest Fest and New Colossus Festival.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">As Prostitute continues work on their sophomore album, they are delving deeper into electronic and Arabic dance influences, drawing inspiration from the ongoing conflicts in Gaza and Lebanon. Their sound continues to evolve, with new tracks incorporating dabke rhythms, Arabesque melodicism, and industrial synth textures, all while retaining the same anarchic energy that defines their unique sound.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Despite its title, Ratboys’ new album Singin’ to an Empty Chair is not defined by what’s missing. Rather, it’s the beginning of an important dialogue with a close loved one vocalist Julia Steiner finds herself estranged from. </p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The music on the band’s sixth studio album – its first for New West Records – fills the space that person left behind with 11 songs showcasing Ratboys at the peak of their powers — twangy, effervescent, as confident as they’ve ever been, and perhaps more emotionally interrogative than ever before. </p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The four-piece Chicago band followed up 2023’s highly acclaimed The Window by reconvening with co-producer Chris Walla to begin tracking at a rural Wisconsin cabin before taking the songs to Steve Albini’s famed Electrical Audio studios in Chicago and later to Rosebud Studio in Evanston, Illinois. </p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The results veer from bubbly power-pop on “Anywhere” to irresistible post-country on “Penny in the Lake,” along with heart-piercing ballads like “Just Want You to Know the Truth” and an exhilarating detour into the extraterrestrial on “Light Night Mountains All That,” which Steiner dubs the band’s mammoth “wormhole jam.” Singin’ to an Empty Chair also marks the first Ratboys album written since Steiner began therapy, which the singer/lyricist credits for the clarity found across the album’s unflinching examinations of relationship and self. Fittingly, as the album begins by extending a hand into the void, it concludes with a scene of serenity – all while weaving candid honesty, humor, chaos, and whimsy along the way. “It's not all doom and gloom,” Steiner says “The experience of making this record definitely gives me hope for whatever happens next.”</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Formed in 2020 in Dearborn, Michigan, Prostitute is an experimental post-punk and Arab rock band. Born out of the isolation of the COVID-19 lockdown, the band’s debut album, Attempted Martyr, was written in the midst of global and personal turmoil, capturing the zeitgeist of a world unraveling. A loose concept record, it chronicles the rise and fall of a doomed zealot whose pursuit of holy vengeance spirals into a psychotic orgy of violence, greed, and lust.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">The band was initially formed by Moe Kazra who enlisted childhood friends Andrew Kaster and Dylan Zaranski, with Ross Babinski and Bret Wall later completing the lineup. Together, they self-funded the album, working with legendary engineer Chris Koltay to shape a sound that's both abrasive and hypnotic—an unrelenting blend of warped guitars, primitive basslines, frenzied drumming, and corrosive synthesizers, interwoven with samples from diverse cultures, ranging from African to Middle Eastern and East Asian influences.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Tracks like “All Hail” (inspired by the 1977 Hanafi Siege of Washington D.C.) immerses listeners in a volatile, hostage-like environment. "Judge" channels Milton's Satan in a chilling rallying cry, while “Body Meat” grapples with religious desperation and the tenuous boundary between faith and madness. Khachab and Kaster’s lyrics have been described by Pitchfork as "disturbingly poetic" with the ability to "lacerate with image alone." Crude sloganeering and scenes of horrific violence are juxtaposed with literary allusion and Islamic symbolism, creating what the band calls a "theatricalization of terrorism." Through this lens, they examine and critique the xenophobic stereotypes targeted at Arabs, distorting them into grotesque caricatures.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">Over the past four years, Prostitute has established a reputation for their punishing, high-energy performances. The band’s live shows, described as “dangerous” and “volatile”, finds Moe delivering politically charged sermons atop a deafening bacchanal of sound. In 2023, Prostitute performed at the re-opening of the iconic UFO Bar in Detroit, followed by a series of benefit concerts for Palestine, Lebanon, and Sudan. These performances solidified their growing presence, leading to invites to play at No Rest Fest and New Colossus Festival.</p><p class="sqsrte-small" style="white-space:pre-wrap;">As Prostitute continues work on their sophomore album, they are delving deeper into electronic and Arabic dance influences, drawing inspiration from the ongoing conflicts in Gaza and Lebanon. Their sound continues to evolve, with new tracks incorporating dabke rhythms, Arabesque melodicism, and industrial synth textures, all while retaining the same anarchic energy that defines their unique sound.</p></div>

  <div class="sqs-html-content" data-sqsp-text-block-content><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">Despite its title, Ratboys’ new album Singin’ to an Empty Chair is not defined by what’s missing. Rather, it’s the beginning of an important dialogue with a close loved one vocalist Julia Steiner finds herself estranged from. </p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The music on the band’s sixth studio album – its first for New West Records – fills the space that person left behind with 11 songs showcasing Ratboys at the peak of their powers — twangy, effervescent, as confident as they’ve ever been, and perhaps more emotionally interrogative than ever before. </p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The four-piece Chicago band followed up 2023’s highly acclaimed The Window by reconvening with co-producer Chris Walla to begin tracking at a rural Wisconsin cabin before taking the songs to Steve Albini’s famed Electrical Audio studios in Chicago and later to Rosebud Studio in Evanston, Illinois. </p><p style="white-space:pre-wrap;" class="sqsrte-small" data-rte-preserve-empty="true">The results veer from bubbly power-pop on “Anywhere” to irresistible post-country on “Penny in the Lake,” along with heart-piercing ballads like “Just Want You to Know the Truth” and an exhilarating detour into the extraterrestrial on “Light Night Mountains All That,” which Steiner dubs the band’s mammoth “wormhole jam.” Singin’ to an Empty Chair also marks the first Ratboys album written since Steiner began therapy, which the singer/lyricist credits for the clarity found across the album’s unflinching examinations of relationship and self. Fittingly, as the album begins by extending a hand into the void, it concludes with a scene of serenity – all while weaving candid honesty, humor, chaos, and whimsy along the way. “It's not all doom and gloom,” Steiner says “The experience of making this record definitely gives me hope for whatever happens next.”</p></div>

Latin Candy: Reggaeton Party

Saturday, 5 September 2026

23:00 — 05:00

E1 London · East London

Buy tickets

// About

After another unforgettable edition, Latin Candy returns this September for a brand-new experience… and this time we’re bringing together the best of Reggaeton & R&B. 🍭🔥

On Saturday 5th September, we’re taking over the legendary E1 London once again, right in the heart of London near Tower Bridge and Tobacco Dock. Famous for its world-class lighting, earth-shaking sound system and hosting some of the biggest events in the city, E1 provides the perfect setting for London’s biggest Reggaeton & R&B party.

Whether you’re coming with your crew, celebrating a birthday, planning the ultimate night out or simply looking for the best Latin party in London, Latin Candy is where you need to be. Expect an electric atmosphere, incredible music and a packed dancefloor from start to finish.

This edition introduces a fresh twist to the Latin Candy experience. Alongside the biggest Reggaeton anthems, we’ll be bringing the smoothest R&B classics and modern favourites into the mix, creating the perfect balance between high-energy Latin rhythms and feel-good singalongs.

From Bad Bunny, Karol G, Feid, Rauw Alejandro and El Alfa to Drake, Chris Brown, Usher, Rihanna, Bryson Tiller, PARTYNEXTDOOR and more, our DJs will be blending the biggest hits, exclusive edits and club anthems all night long. Expect seamless transitions, huge moments and non-stop energy until the lights come on.

As always, Latin Candy brings more than just music. Expect immersive production, vibrant visuals, signature candy-themed décor and a crowd that knows exactly how to party. Every edition has its own unique atmosphere, and this September promises to be one of our biggest yet.

What to expect:

🍭 London’s biggest Reggaeton & R&B party

🔥 The ultimate mix of Reggaeton, R&B, Dembow & Latin club edits

🎧 London’s top DJs playing non-stop anthems all night

💃 A packed dancefloor with incredible energy

✨ Stunning production, visuals & signature Latin Candy décor

🎉 Birthday celebrations, special surprises & unforgettable moments

🌃 One of London’s most iconic nightlife venues – E1 London

Dress to impress, bring your best energy and get ready for a night you’ll be talking about long after it’s ends.

This isn’t just another night out. This is Latin Candy. 🍭🔥

records.description:
There are DJs, and then there are people who are simply part of of club culture Fat Tony is firmly in the latter camp. DJ, promoter, writer and lifelong student of the dancefloor, he came up through the kind of London nightlife where the lines between the club, the afterparty and the rest of life were never particularly clear. That distinctly British way of raving, a little rough around the edges, a lot of personality, and always about the music, runs deep through everything he does.

On 5 September, he makes his E1 debut, joining our favourite brothers, The Menendez Brother

<h1 class="tribe-events-single-event-title">Bow Open x Mile End Community Project presents ‘to belong’</h1>		
<div id="post-26138" class="post-26138 tribe_events type-tribe_events status-publish has-post-thumbnail hentry tag-exhibition tag-nunnery-gallery tribe_events_cat-exhibitions location-bow-road cat_exhibitions">
	<div class="tribe-events-schedule tribe-clearfix">
	<h2 class="tribe-events-schedule__datetime"> 
				Friday 5th June 2026 – Sunday  30th August 2026			 
, 10:00am to 4:00pm	

			
	</h2>
</div>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-medium-font-size">Our annual Bow Open exhibition platforms work from Bow Arts artists, showing new and innovative work selected by a different guest curator each year. This year, the Nunnery Gallery is working with young curators from Mile End Community Project (MCP) to deliver a truly multi-perspective and dynamic show. </h2>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="683" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-1024x683.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-28940" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-1024x683.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-300x200.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-768x512.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-1536x1024.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-2048x1366.jpg 2048w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-1080x720.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-1920x1281.jpg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-600x400.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Bow-Open-2026-Nunnery-Gallery.-Photo-by-Rob-Harris-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-18-960x640.jpg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Various Artists from Bow Open 2026 at Nunnery Gallery. Photo by Rob Harris, Courtesy of Bow Arts  </figcaption></figure>



<p class="has-lgrey-background-color has-background wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Exhibition opening hours:</strong> <br>Wednesday – Sunday, 10am – 4pm</p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">Featuring</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>Rômulo Avi, Joy Baek, Mark Beldan, Victoria Burgher, Eleanor Burkett, Tom Coates, Chloe Cooper, Samuel Donagh, Ioana Elecfi, Roxana Gutila, Lucile Haefflinger, Ruiji Han, Yifan He, Jonny Kemp, Niki Kohandel, John Lord, Maria Stella Lydaki, Nicola McEvoy, Shrub Mostert, Alison P. O’Reilly, Charlotte Parr Burman, Sophie Popper, Anaïs Serres, Tara Versey, Denisa Zajacova</em></p>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading">‘to belong’</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">What does it mean to belong? Is it a place, a person, a feeling? Is it an individual experience, or something we share? What happens when that sense of belonging is lost, and how do we find it again?</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">This year’s Bow Open brings together work from 25 artists centred around the theme of belonging, selected by young curators Mara Ahmed, Justine Enyan, Eleanor Getting and Lydia Lott with Mile End Community Project. Showcasing artists from across Bow Arts’ community, the exhibition presents many artforms, including painting, print, sculpture and video, all a testament to how belonging is a practice, rooted in place, identity, memory and community.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Visitors can explore the accompanying event programme, including artist workshops and an evening takeover from our young curators and event programmers, below.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Guided tours of the exhibition led by the young curators will take place during <a href="https://bowarts.org/event/bowfest-open-studios/">Bowfest: Bow Road Open Studios</a>.</p>

<h2 class="wp-block-heading">More about Mile End Community Project</h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Mile End Community Project is an award-winning youth and community organisation with an established reputation for creative projects. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">MCP is an award-winning youth and community organisation with an established reputation for creative and innovative projects. Since 1995 they have delivered a range of social and educational activities for Tower Hamlets residents who may not otherwise engage due to social, cultural, racial or economic challenges. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">More about <a href="https://www.mileendcommunityproject.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Mile End Community Project</a>.  </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Access Information</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Nunnery Gallery and Cafe have step-free access throughout from street level, including to the accessible toilet, and is service animal friendly. This venue does not have a hearing loop system.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Accessible parking is not available on-site but blue badge parking can be found 500m away on Fairfield Road.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">If you have any questions regarding accessibility at this venue or event, would like to make us aware of any access requirements that you have in advance of visiting, or would like this information in an alternate format including Easy Read, please email <a href="mailto:nunnery@bowarts.com" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">nunnery@bowarts.com</a> or call 020 8980 7774 (Ext. 3)</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Access requirements could include things like providing equipment, services or support (e.g. information in Easy Read, speech to text software, additional 1:1 support), adjusting workshop timings (e.g. more break times), adjustments to the event space (e.g. making sure you have a table near the entrance) or anything else you can think of!)</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Opening hours: </strong>Wed-Sun, 10am to 4pm</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Address:</strong> Nunnery Gallery, 181 Bow Road, London, E3 2SJ</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Nearest station(s):</strong> Bow Road (District and Hammersmith and City lines) is a 6-minute walk away, and Bow Church (DLR) is a 3-minute walk away.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bus:</strong> 205, 25, 425, A8, D8, 108, 276, 488 and 8 all service the surrounding area.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Bike:</strong> Bicycle parking is located at Bow Church Station. The nearest Santander Cycles docking station is at Bow Church Station.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Lakeside Centre’s annual Open Studios is coming up this September! Meet the artists working in the studios, and see inside their artistic practices–ranging from painting and costuming, to analogue photography and more. Alongside the Open Studios, there will be a host of activities and entertainments to book on the day. Look out at the Southmere Lake from the roof of the building, or make new memories with loved ones inside.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">For the fourth year running, the Open Studios is taking place as part of Open City’s Open House Festival, celebrating our curiosity for what happens inside the buildings that we walk past every day. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The 1960’s iconic brutalist building was <a href="https://bowarts.org/bow-arts-lakeside-centre-shortlisted-for-the-pineapples-awards/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">nominated for a Pineapple award</a> for its sustainable creative retrofit, and has also featured as the backdrop for films such as <em>Beautiful Thing</em> and the TV series <em>Misfits</em>. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-extra-large-font-size">Explore the event programme</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Throughout the day, we’ve organised a series of workshops with artists from Thamesmead to keep the day buzzing. Book your ticket below in advance to make sure you get a spot.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" width="1024" height="762" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-1024x762.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29691" style="aspect-ratio:1.3441680210026252" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-1024x762.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-300x223.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-768x572.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-1536x1143.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-1080x804.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-1920x1429.jpg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-600x446.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0-960x714.jpg 960w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image0.jpg 2048w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>



<div class="wp-block-pb-accordion-item c-accordion__item js-accordion-item no-js" data-initially-open="false" data-click-to-close="true" data-auto-close="true" data-scroll="false" data-scroll-offset="0"><h2 id="at-92720" class="c-accordion__title js-accordion-controller" role="button">12pm & 3pm | Workshop: Marbling with Chloe Cooper </h2><div id="ac-92720" class="c-accordion__content">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>12-2pm & 3-5pm | Free | Drop-in</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Join artist educator Chloe Cooper for a playful marbling workshop inspired by Thamesmead’s stories. You will use coloured paint and a variety of tools to swirl and shape colourful patterns, then print your designs onto different coloured papers, including pages featuring articles from historic editions of the <em>Thamesmead Times</em>. Discover the magic of printmaking, experiment with colour and movement, and create unique artworks inspired by the local community’s past.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Please note, this workshop is suitable for children age 8+.</p>
</div></div>



<div class="wp-block-pb-accordion-item c-accordion__item js-accordion-item no-js" data-initially-open="false" data-click-to-close="true" data-auto-close="true" data-scroll="false" data-scroll-offset="0"><h2 id="at-92721" class="c-accordion__title js-accordion-controller" role="button">12pm | Workshop: Making Places – Stories of Thamesmead </h2><div id="ac-92721" class="c-accordion__content">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>12-1:30pm | Free | Drop-in</strong></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full is-resized"><img decoding="async" width="386" height="217" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Sam-Williams-Lakeside-Image.png" alt="" class="wp-image-29662" style="aspect-ratio:1.778900821225521;width:646px;height:auto" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Sam-Williams-Lakeside-Image.png 386w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Sam-Williams-Lakeside-Image-300x169.png 300w" sizes="(max-width: 386px) 100vw, 386px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Everyone has a story to tell. And from street corners to mountaintops, places are the stage on which the stories of our lives unfold. Throughout history, telling stories has been how people maintain a sense of belonging and continuity through times of transition. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Through examples and simple techniques – from TV, poetry, journalism and video games – this workshop is an opportunity to develop a piece of writing inspired by a place that matters to you. No experience required. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>
</div></div>



<div class="wp-block-pb-accordion-item c-accordion__item js-accordion-item no-js" data-initially-open="false" data-click-to-close="true" data-auto-close="true" data-scroll="false" data-scroll-offset="0"><h2 id="at-92722" class="c-accordion__title js-accordion-controller" role="button">1pm | Workshop: Clear Your Mind with Roni Parker </h2><div id="ac-92722" class="c-accordion__content">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>1-3pm | Free | Drop-in</strong></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large is-resized"><img decoding="async" width="1024" height="683" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-1024x683.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29621" style="aspect-ratio:1.4992888417882142;width:631px;height:auto" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-1024x683.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-300x200.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-768x512.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-1536x1025.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-2048x1366.jpg 2048w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-1080x720.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-1920x1281.jpg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-600x400.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-146-960x640.jpg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Lakeside Open Studios 2025. Image credit: Alberto Romano</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Discover how you can produce beautiful pieces of art from your kitchen table, that not only look good, but give your head some time out.  </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Join Roni Parker in her studio and learn just how easy it is to build some calming, creative space into your busy life and get your creative juices flowing. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"> No experience required – just come play! All welcome. </p>
</div></div>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-extra-large-font-size">Visit our Studio Activities</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Alongside the workshop programme, explore the artist-led activities inside the studios.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" width="1024" height="777" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1-1024x777.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29685" style="aspect-ratio:1.31790547166111" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1-1024x777.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1-300x228.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1-768x583.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1-1536x1166.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1-1080x820.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1-600x455.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1-960x729.jpg 960w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Miyuki1-1.jpg 1920w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption"><em>Can you hear us? </em>Miyuki Kasahara</figcaption></figure>



<div class="wp-block-pb-accordion-item c-accordion__item js-accordion-item no-js" data-initially-open="false" data-click-to-close="true" data-auto-close="true" data-scroll="false" data-scroll-offset="0"><h2 id="at-92725" class="c-accordion__title js-accordion-controller" role="button">Installation: <em>Can you hear us?</em> by Miyuki Kasahara</h2><div id="ac-92725" class="c-accordion__content">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Free | Drop-in | Suitable for all ages</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Miyuki Kasahara’s installation <em>Can you hear us? </em>leads you on a trail around the Lakeside garden to follow a conversation between plants and insects. Through dialogue on wooden speech bubbles, you will hear about how communication has been disturbed by pollution, how mobile phone traffic has messed up mapping signals, and how pesticide has become so addictive.</p>
</div></div>



<div class="wp-block-pb-accordion-item c-accordion__item js-accordion-item no-js" data-initially-open="false" data-click-to-close="true" data-auto-close="true" data-scroll="false" data-scroll-offset="0"><h2 id="at-92726" class="c-accordion__title js-accordion-controller" role="button"><em>Swoop Together</em> with J.D. Swann</h2><div id="ac-92726" class="c-accordion__content">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Free | Drop-in | Suitable for all ages</strong></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" width="1024" height="724" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-1024x724.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29619" style="aspect-ratio:1.4143759168314305" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-1024x724.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-300x212.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-768x543.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-1536x1086.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-2048x1448.jpg 2048w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-1080x764.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-1920x1357.jpg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-600x424.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Common-Swift-Calum-F-Kerr-and-many-more-960x679.jpg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">On lucky days between April/May and September when the clouds are low, colonies of Common Swifts fly over the Lakeside Centre feeding off the insects by Southmere Lake. However, these most high-flying and far travelling of birds are in trouble due to lack of breeding sites and climatic changes.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Swoop together in the studio to decorate the Common Swift there with messages to or drawings of these threatened birds. All materials provided.</p>
</div></div>



<div class="wp-block-pb-accordion-item c-accordion__item js-accordion-item no-js" data-initially-open="false" data-click-to-close="true" data-auto-close="true" data-scroll="false" data-scroll-offset="0"><h2 id="at-92727" class="c-accordion__title js-accordion-controller" role="button">12pm & 2pm | 1-2-1 Chats: Developing and nurturing ideas for artistic and creative endeavours with Jasmine Haskell</h2><div id="ac-92727" class="c-accordion__content">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Drop into the artist studio between <strong>12-1pm</strong> and <strong>2-4pm</strong>. On arrival, please sign up on the timesheet to secure your slot! </p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img decoding="async" width="1024" height="683" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-1024x683.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29726" style="aspect-ratio:1.4992052204467499" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-1024x683.jpg 1024w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-300x200.jpg 300w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-768x512.jpg 768w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-1536x1025.jpg 1536w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-2048x1366.jpg 2048w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-1080x720.jpg 1080w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-1920x1281.jpg 1920w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-600x400.jpg 600w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/LakesideCentre-OpenStudios2025-Photo-Alberto-Romano-Courtesy-of-Bow-Arts-35-960x640.jpg 960w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Lakeside Open Studios 2025. Image credit: Alberto Romano</figcaption></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Join Jasmine Haskell, a local creative small business owner, for a one-on-one chat about developing and nurturing ideas for artistic and creative endeavours. These 20-minute time slots will offer a sounding board for discussing that little thought you’ve had in the back of your mind, and how to bring it into the world with a tangible and scalable approach. This is also an opportunity to pick Jasmine’s mind about practical details like the logistics of ecommerce, picking a business name, planning a logo, and what makes a business idea viable. </p>
</div></div>

<div class="wp-block-pb-accordion-item c-accordion__item js-accordion-item no-js" data-initially-open="false" data-click-to-close="true" data-auto-close="true" data-scroll="false" data-scroll-offset="0"><h3 id="at-92728" class="c-accordion__title js-accordion-controller" role="button">12-6pm | On the Wall</h3><div id="ac-92728" class="c-accordion__content">
<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Project Space (second floor) | Free | Drop-in</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Encounter landscape from an uncommon perspective – one shaped by touch, movement, and collaboration.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><em>On the Wall</em> explores how physical movement through the landscape shapes artistic process, offering audiences an intimate perspective on Britain’s and Spain’s climbing environments and the communities that inhabit them.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A collaborative exhibition bringing together Thamesmead basedpainter Alexander Heaton and photographer Jonathan Blower. Their work explores climbing as more than a subject – it is a way of seeing.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The exhibition will be open on selected dates until Saturday 3rd October.</p>

</div>
</div></div>

<h3 class="wp-block-heading has-wpdc-extra-large-font-size">Activities from our Neighbours & Partners</h3>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We’ve partnered with local friends to bring a taste of what they offer to the Lakeside Centre.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full is-resized"><img decoding="async" width="451" height="338" src="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Thamesmead-Sharks.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-29680" style="aspect-ratio:1.33433498220147;width:840px;height:auto" srcset="https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Thamesmead-Sharks.jpg 451w, https://bowarts.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Thamesmead-Sharks-300x225.jpg 300w" sizes="(max-width: 451px) 100vw, 451px" /></figure>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Located just beside the Lakeside Centre, The Sharks will be open on the day offering paddling sessions at Southmere Water Sport Centre. Sessions are suitable for all skill levels and are designed as a gentle way to get new people paddling and experienced paddlers more active. Children ages 4 years old to school Year 3 will need to have a parent take them in a double kayak.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Sessions are every 45 minutes, £7 per session.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Find out more about how to fix and mend small electrical items at our Thamesmead Repair café stall. Get advice and learn some top tips. </p>

records.title: Bow Skills workshop: re-imagining city landscapes with poetry and wandering with Jazzy Green
records.description: <p>Every day we walk our urban city scape with stories and poetry flying past us, unnoticed. How does our culture of productivity and routine thieve our ability to notice and re-imagine everyday ephemera around us? Join poet Jazzy Green for an accessible writing workshop open to anyone with an interest in poetry and movement as creative practice.</p>\n

records.title: Bow Skills workshop: bid writing and arts fundraising with Kim Pearce – an Arts Council England special!
records.description: <p>Join experienced arts fundraiser Kim Pearce in this Arts Council England (ACE) project grants special, as she demystifies the four investment principles, breaks down the application structure, and provides practical insights into how to build out a successful ACE bid.  The workshop will end with a Q&A where you can put your burning questions to Kim about specific ideas or issues you’re coming up against! </p>\n

observations.description: Explore the 38 artist studios located inside the Lakeside Centre and join Bow Arts for a day of exhibitions, and family-friendly workshops.

observations.title: Yoga Sessions at the Lakeside Centre
observations.description: <p>Amanda Eatwell will be returning this summer to teach her much-loved yoga sessions, located on the stunning Lakeside Centre rooftop.</p>\n

observations.title: RCRDSHOP Live Lounge at Oaklands Social
observations.description: <p>Join London’s finest soul and hip hop music collective, RCRDSHOP as they once again take over Oaklands Social. Enjoy an evening of London’s best emerging artists playing alongside the RCRDSHOP live band. </p>\n

observations.title: Bow Families: creating your own puppet deities with Nicola McEvoy
observations.description: <p>Join artist Nicola McEvoy to make different mythological creatures or deities and work collectively to make a shared ‘chimera’ – a monster composed of many animals.</p>\n

observations.title: Knitting the Air: The Exhibition
observations.description: <p>Knitting the Air presents a free exhibition exploring air pollution, place, and community made by 132 knitters from across Poplar, Bow and wider east London.</p>\n

observations.title: Yoga Sessions at the Lakeside Centre
observations.description: <p>Amanda Eatwell will be returning this summer to teach her much-loved yoga sessions, located on the stunning Lakeside Centre rooftop.</p>\n

observations.title: Bow Skills workshop: re-imagining city landscapes with poetry and wandering with Jazzy Green
observations.description: <p>Every day we walk our urban city scape with stories and poetry flying past us, unnoticed. How does our culture of productivity and routine thieve our ability to notice and re-imagine everyday ephemera around us? Join poet Jazzy Green for an accessible writing workshop open to anyone with an interest in poetry and movement as creative practice.</p>\n

observations.title: Thamesmead Wildlife Wanders: Autumn Walk with J D Swann
observations.description: <p>A seasonal wildlife walk in Thamesmead with ornithological investigator J D Swann, with an emphasis on observation of birds, local ecology and history.</p>\n

observations.title: Community Outdoor Cinema: Disney’s Encanto at Royal Albert Wharf
observations.description: <p>Join us on the dock for a free outdoor cinema screening of Disney’s Encanto! Grab a pair of our cinema headphones, settle into a deck chair, grab some popcorn, and enjoy a magical evening by the water with family, friends, and neighbours of all ages as we celebrate the end of summer together at Royal Albert Wharf.  </p>\n

observations.title: Bow Skills workshop: bid writing and arts fundraising with Kim Pearce – an Arts Council England special!
observations.description: <p>Join experienced arts fundraiser Kim Pearce in this Arts Council England (ACE) project grants special, as she demystifies the four investment principles, breaks down the application structure, and provides practical insights into how to build out a successful ACE bid.  The workshop will end with a Q&A where you can put your burning questions to Kim about specific ideas or issues you’re coming up against! </p>\n

observations.title: Lakeside Centre Performance Evening
observations.description: <p>Join us at the Lakeside Centre for a dynamic and collaborative evening of performance. Led by artist Joanna Penso, and featuring work by multidisciplinary artist Gusty Ferro, explore performance through an undiscovered lens.</p>\n

observations.title: On the Wall Exhibition
observations.description: <p>Encounter landscape from an uncommon perspective - one shaped by touch, movement, and collaboration.</p>\n

Future Curators Programme

DASH, Disability Arts Online, John Hansard Gallery, MAC Birmingham, MIMA, (Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art), Newlyn Art Gallery & The Exchange, Wysing Arts Centre, 15/8/2025 – 1/3/2027 #Sheffield #Curator Residency

Drafts film still (2025) directed by Jade Foster. Cinematographer: Freddy Griffiths
Back to top

Arts Catalyst is proud to be part of the Future Curators Programme

The Future Curators Programme 2023-2026 is a residency programme for Disabled curators within mainstream visual arts institutions. 

Grounded in Disability Justice, the Future Curators Programme was founded by Disabled artist-led visual arts organisation, DASH, and is run in partnership with: Arts Catalyst, Disability Arts Online, John Hansard Gallery, MAC Birmingham, MIMA (Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art), Newlyn Art Gallery & The Exchange, and Wysing Arts Centre.

Using an action research approach and a multiplicity of intersectional lived experiences, DASH, FCP partners, and resident curators collaborate on programmes, system change, evaluation, commissions, and critical thinking so Disability Justice is embodied in their practice.

 

Drafts (2025)

DASH curator Jade Foster directed a film titled “Drafts”, it sets the intentions for the programme. Foster utilised the project as a testing ground to treat ‘communication’ as a subject and material, an aesthetic and a politic, challenging normative communication styles by  producing an artistic approach to communication that goes beyond traditional attitudes towards access.

[soft liquid keys chime nostalgically] at the beginning of the film, setting a textured tone of liquidity, reflection and softness. Following the director’s rough cut and a conversation about the sound of language with Foster, Axel Kacoutié, an award-winning audio artist and poet, produced a responsive score based on their intuition and gut knowledge. Disabled and queer-led working group Carefuffle in London then penned the captions in an eb-and flo collaborative process, communicating the nuance of Kacoutié’s vision. Their creative captioning, throughout the work, responds to musical texture, voice, non-verbal communication, and visuality. It incorporates animations, symbols, directional changes, as well as variations in typeface, colour and rhythm. This approach builds from the methodological bedrock developed for Drafts by Collective Text, a Glasgow-based, Disabled and Deaf artist-led organisation.

Following a young Black masc in rural England, we come across new growth amongst browned leaves as we spiritually enter Spring. Just as language attempts to resist capture through its opacity, so does the boi, whose future is ahead of him if only the sector would allow it. You know, if the industry doesn’t try to split him, forcing apart melanin and disability, like trying to separate leaves from soil.

Split. Splinting between experience and articulation.

Hands call to us; call out and reground us. The hands of the teenager, Muslim, British South Asian, Deaf actor Sahera Khan, and Black Deaf actor David Ellington remind us to show up for the living and the future. Their hands are followed by those of Heather Peak (DASH), reciting their ‘draft’ as a synesthetic drawing to declare, embody, and deposit their intentions for Future Curators Programme (FCP) and how they are feeling their way through the process. Peak is proceeded by ‘drafts’ from Claudia Lastra (Arts Catalyst), Elinor Morgan (Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art, MIMA), Roma Piotrowska (Midlands Arts Centre), Trish Wheatley (Disability Arts Online), James Green (Newlyn Art Gallery & The Exchange), and Rosie Cooper (Wysing Arts Centre).

In the face of prevailing austerity, we are proud to recommit ourselves to leading change. Launched in August 2025 via a simultaneous digital release across eight partner organisations, including DASH, Drafts brings together the individual and organisational voices of directors and curators from seven influential contemporary visual arts organisations across England to create a constellation of vision and mission statements for the Future Curators Programme (FCP).

A note on the different versions of Drafts: ‘For the film director, sound without dialogue or non-auditory languages (touch, symbols, and drawing) is easier for them to process. Noise, sound and music speak to them, and they consider the sound score as a form of communication in its own right. Additionally, Carefuffle and Jade decided together that witnessing BSL without subtitles was affirming because it’s also a language in its own right, and a beautifully embodied one. There are different approaches to signing, and we wanted to highlight the complexity of BSL. Therefore, we have also provided a written transcript for those who wish to engage further with its complexity.’

Download the Drafts BSL Transcript and the Press Release above.

If possible, listen to the film through headphones.

Credits

Director: Jade Foster

Cinematographer: Freddy Griffiths

Film Composer: Axel Kacoutié

Cast: Joshua Samuel, Sahera Khan and David Ellington; Heather Peak, Claudia Lastra, Elinor Morgan, Roma Piotrowska, Trish Wheatley, James Green, and Rosie Cooper

Caption Groundwork: Collective Text

Captioning Consultant (Collective Text): Bea Webster

Creative Captioning: Carefuffle

Captioning Consultant (Carefuffle): Nina Thomas

Audio Description: SoundScribe and Jade Foster

SoundScribe Visual Awareness Consultant: Kirin Saeed

Production Assistant: Lucy Mounfield

DASH Team (Production Support): Esther Cartwright and Rachel Fleming-Mulford

Location: Wysing Arts Centre

 

About the Director

Jade Foster (they/them) is a British curatorial and business consultant, artist and art historian of Afro-Caribbean heritage living in Yarm, North Yorkshire. They are currently a Curator at Primary in Nottingham and was a Curator at DASH. At DASH, they curated their system change work, including The DASH Library and the Future Curators Programme (FCP), a consortium and residency programme for Disabled curators within seven visual arts institutions across the UK. Recently, they made their directorial debut with Drafts (2025). Previously, Foster has worked with artist filmmakers such as Sonya Dyer, Maybelle Peters, Jala Wahid, and Matthew Arthur Williams. And has an interest in Latin American and Caribbean-descended modern and contemporary art, writing about the film practices of Carolyn Lazard, Lygia Pape, Anna Maria Maiolino, and, in recent years, Alberta Whittle for LUX.

 

What will happen during the Future Curators Programme?

As part of the programme, each partner will host a residency with a disabled/neurodivergent curator. As a member of the network, Arts Catalyst has monthly peer sharing and learning meetings, working groups, and DASH have developed homework and training for the cohort.

Arts Catalyst has partnered with DAO (Disability Arts Online) to accommodate a residency over a 15 month period with Curator Nathalie Boobis. After a recruitment process in Autumn 2024, Nathalie joined DAO as Curator of dis_place, the organisation’s new accessible digital gallery space which launched in May 2025.

Nathalie will begin her residency with Arts Catalyst in early 2026 with an outcome of the residency taking place in Spring 2027.

Trish Wheatley, CEO, Disability Arts Online: 

“It is an amazing opportunity for me to be supported as part of FCP to develop a year-long programme at Arts Catalyst. To have the resources, mentorship and space to think with and through the work of disabled artists will be pivotal to my practice and how this work feeds back into the sector.”

Nathalie Boobis, Curator, Disability Arts Online:

“It is an amazing opportunity for me to be supported as part of FCP to develop a year-long programme at Arts Catalyst. To have the resources, mentorship and space to think with and through the work of disabled artists will be pivotal to my practice and how this work feeds back into the sector.”

Claudia Lastra, CEO, Arts Catalyst:

“We are thrilled to be partnering with Disability Arts Online, a pioneering force in championing disabled voices within the cultural sector. Their work continues to lead the way in arts and disability. We’re especially excited to support Nathalie and her curatorial vision for the programme.”

 

Why is this important and why now? Our vision for the programme

With peers and through the process of the Future Curator’s Programme we will learn, share, and explore our mission for the programme.

For Arts Catalyst, the Future Curators Programme is about dismantling barriers, reimagining power structures, and building a community rooted in solidarity and collective care. This is not just about accessibility, it’s about revolutionising who gets to curate, create, and lead. 

We are committed to platforming disabled and neurodivergent voices, not as an afterthought, but as the driving force in reshaping the arts. This is about more than inclusion; it’s about reclaiming space and redefining what curatorial practice can be.

 

Supporting disabled curators and artists

It is crucial to support disabled curators and artists, especially in light of the UK government’s current plans to cut disability benefits by £5 billion a year, the largest cuts on record. 

These cuts would be catastrophic for disabled people’s living standards and independence. Disabled people are not a small minority; they make up 23% of the working-age population, rising to 36% when including those with long-term health conditions. Living with a disability often comes with significant extra costs, Scope’s 2024 report found that disabled households need an additional £1,010 per month to reach the same standard of living as non-disabled households. Yet, disabled people face lower employment rates and earn far less when in work.  

Source: Unlimited

 

Early musings on the transformative potentials of wobbly and unreasonable crip time shapes
