Soil Futures

21/7/2022 – 16/12/2023 #Indonesia #Italy #Palestine #Artist Residency #Programme

Back to top

Soil Futures was a network of creative organisations exploring the ground between us.

Soil Futures was a collaboration between five organisations: Arts Catalyst (Sheffield, UK); RIWAQ (al Bireh, Palestine); Sakiya – Art/Science/Agriculture (Ein Qiniya, Palestine); Struggles for Sovereignty (Yogyakarta, Indonesia); and Vessel Art Project (Puglia, Italy). 

Soil Futures traversed the practices of five organisations whose work happens in collaboration with communities within their local contexts: from combining agrarian traditions with contemporary ecological practices, to organising across art, food, land rights, indigenous and ecological activism; from monitoring pollution to connecting with wetlands through sound and different ways of sensing. 

Over the course of one year, this collective endeavour took the shape of a programme featuring an artist residency exchange, an online school, a podcast, and a season of distributed local gatherings. 

Grounded within the localities where each organisation is based, this hybrid programme created an intercultural exchange between artists, ecologists, activists, and soil caretakers to collectively mobilise existing and future knowledges of soil. 

Soil Futures viewed soil and those looking after it (human and non-human) as active agents of change and resistance in the face of current geopolitical and environmental crises.

The project asked: What nutrients are necessary for soils to thrive? What practices of care and maintenance are enacted across different territories and cultures? What ecological knowledges and approaches nourish both lands and communities?

Artist Residency

Following an open call launched in September 2022, the Soil Futures artist research residency was awarded to artist Raghad Saqfalhait, Marie Hervé, and artist collective Al-Wah’at.

As part of the residency, the artists had the opportunity to delve into rural contexts in Palestine (Marie Hervé and Al-Wah’at) and Southern Italy (Raghad Saqfalhait) and to work closely with organisations that operate at the intersection of art, agro-ecology and environmental practices while being responsive to their regional ecologies.

Some of these experiences and learnings were gathered together by Bint Mbareh through a podcast featuring the voices of the artists. The artists reflected on their research residencies and the landscapes, stories, and people they encountered: Raghad delves into her work with clay between Al-Jib in Palestine and Salento in Southern Italy; Marie describes the time she spent with stones and the stories they tell in Qalandiya, near Jerusalem; Al-Wah’at share their collaborative work in Ein Qiniya contemplating the significance of the prickly pear and the cochineal insect for the Palestinian land. 

About the Artists

Al-Wah’at Collective is an artist research collective formed by Ailo Ribas, Gabriella Demczuk, and Areej Ashhab. The collective is committed to growing communal practices in ecologies typically regarded as hostile and lifeless, and to countering human-centred and colonial narratives around arid lands and futures. Al-Wah’at experiment with archival research, on-the-ground fieldwork, material experimentation and image-making through practices of care and knowledge exchange across the human and more-than-human.

In 2023, the collective embarked on their project Wild Hedges at Sakiya organisation in Ein Qiniya, Palestine, as part of the Soil Futures residency program organised by Arts Catalyst and funded by the British Council. The project, winning the COAL 2023 Prize, studies and works with the ecological and socio-political complexities of the prickly pear cactus and the cochineal insect across multiple geographies, communities, and temporalities.

Raghad Saqfalhait is a Palestinian artist and designer currently based in Eindhoven. With a background in architecture, she explores material cultures and craft ecologies through hands-on experimentation and field research, collaborating with partners across diverse fields including environmental sciences, archaeology, and local communities. Her work centers soil as both a subject and a methodology, revealing its entanglements with histories of extraction, land dispossession, and settler colonialism.

In 2019, she co-founded Sakeb, a design collective working on, about, and through waste—particularly that produced by the limestone industry. Her practice extends into performance and moving image, including The Geography of Pottery (2022), La Montagna è Ancora in Movimento (2023), and The Dead Are Never Inertرماد مسكون (2026). Raghad is a recipient of the Prince Claus Seed Award (2022), and recently graduated with a Master’s in Geo-Design from the Design Academy Eindhoven (2026). 

Originally from Marseille and trained in philosophy of aesthetics, Marie Hervé graduated from the Ecole Nationale Supérieure de la Photographie d’Arles in 2020. Her practice brings together writing, image-making, experimental printing and installation. Her research focuses on Southern territories and their neo-colonial ghosts, approaching historical constructions as hauntings or spectropoetic forms. Based between Rome and Marseille, she works primarily in collaboration with French artist Elsa Martinez. Their work has received several awards, including the Eurazeo Creation Grant in 2021, the CNAP Documentary Photography Support Grant in 2025, and the Polycopies & Co Grant in 2026, supporting their upcoming monograph Que le feu soit tendre, que la mer soit bonne, published by C. Editions.

She has held solo exhibitions at FRAC Sud (Marseille), unRepresented by Approche (Paris), Galerie F. (Senlis), Fujikina Arles with Fuji x Fisheye (Rencontres d’Arles), Polyptyque (Marseille), Muta Gallery (Turin), Campo Aperto (Rome), as well as at AKC Museum (New York), Portuense201 Gallery (Rome), the 69th edition of the Salon de Montrouge (Paris) and Una Vetrina (Rome).

She has taken part in research residencies such as Nuovo Grand Tour of the Institut Français Italia, A Natural Oasis? Residency (Miramar Network), Soil Futures Residency exchange (Palestine), and The Inherited Earth residency – FE26 (Tinos, Greece), as well as the Futures Photography program upon invitation by Der Greif, Création en cours program of Ateliers Médicis and Hypermaremma – Hyperesidencies in 2026. 

Bint Mbareh is a sound researcher with a focus on water in Palestine. Her interest in the physical parallel between the water wave and the sound wave leads her into questions of border dissolutions (between bodies, between states, between tenses), and into the possibility of being enveloped by the voice, by sounding communally similar to being enveloped by a water body. She challenges Settler colonial epistemology by taking seriously Palestinian ways of knowing, from rain-summoning music to shrine pilgrimage as an instigator to political revolution. Bint Mbareh recently performed vocal activation workshops at Unsound Festival (2024) and London Refugee Week (2024).

About the Organisations

Vessel Art Project

Vessel is a nomadic curatorial organisation and agency invested in supporting artistic and curatorial practices that are situated, responsive and research-led.

Driven by a biographical and epistemological belonging to the South – Southern European and Mediterranean regions in particular – and embedded in an ongoing act of hosting and being hosted, Vessel’s practice manifests itself through public programming, commissioning and writing. In the last 11 years Vessel has participated and contributed to shaping an understanding of curatorial practice connected to a locale (or locality) though not by default based within it.

Far from representing the rural identity of this region through a nostalgic approach and through the myth of an exotic slow life, over the past ten years Vessel has sought to enhance the complexity of this territory and of its histories – from the impact of the fascist territorial plans that have deeply modified the configuration of the area to the effects of monoculture on impoverished soils and often exploitative farming industries – by activating a dialogue between a multiplicity of viewpoints, particularly those seeking other ways of being rural.

Riwaq – Centre for Architectural Conservation

Riwaq – Centre for Architectural Conservation is an NGO established in 1991 in an effort to preserve the cultural heritage in Palestine — it was the preservation of peasants’ architecture and cultural heritage that influenced the centre’s agenda and vision for 30 years. In 2017 Riwaq initiated its project in rural Jerusalem ‘The life Jacket: The Restoration and Regeneration of Rural Jerusalem’, rendering the villages surrounding the city of Jerusalem – with their agricultural produce, their labour force, and services – a sort of “life jacket” to the city itself.

Sakiya

Sakiya is a progressive academy for experimental knowledge production and sharing, grafting local agrarian traditions of self-sufficiency with contemporary art and ecological practices. This circular system of knowledge production and sharing integrates agriculture within the framework of an interdisciplinary residency programme, where cultural actors, such as farmers and crafts/small industry initiatives, assume a prominent role alongside visiting and local artists and scholars. Sakiya’s core programs engage food production, exhibitions, symposia, publications, and education/training workshops, exploring the intersections between art, science, and agriculture in a sustainable and replicable model.

Struggles for Sovereignty

Struggles for Sovereignty, Land, Water, Farming, Food (SFS) is a collective platform focusing on the intersections of social & ecological justice, organised by Bodies of Power / Power for Bodies and Bakudapan Food Study Group, based in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. They develop programs both online and offline that bring together communities working from the fields of art, food, farming, land rights, indigenous (“adat”) and ecological activism to share their work and contexts with each other and the public. Through their programs, they aim to build lasting solidarity between groups in Indonesia and around the world who are engaged with struggles for the right to self-determination over the basic resources that our individual and collective bodies need.

Soil Futures is funded by the British Council’s International Collaboration Grants, which are designed to support UK and overseas organisations to collaborate on international arts projects.

Cydonia Knights – The UK’s Definitive MUSE Tribute

Cydonia Knights are the UK’s longest running and most-followed MUSE tribute, with over a decade of live shows and festival appearances across the UK and Europe

they’ve cemented their place as the UK's ultimate Muse experience.

Formed by Muse fans, for Muse fans, this 3-piece recreation of The Teignmouth Trio delivers a live show of MUSE classics, including Plug In Baby, Hysteria, Starlight, Knights Of Cydonia, New Born, Assassin, Supermassive Black Hole, Uprising, Unravelling and more – all performed with precision and passion.

With synchronized lighting, video visuals, and authentic stage presence, Cydonia Knights nail the sound, look, and energy of MUSE in every performance.

				<h1>TAKING UP SPACE:</h1>
<h2>A BOLD AND UNAPOLOGETIC UPRISING OF BLACK & BROWN QUEER POWER</h2>
<p>August 1st – 31st 2026</p>
<p>This summer, TAKING UP SPACE arrives with unapologetic power and presence, in this ground-breaking photography exhibition centring Black and Brown Queer voices, stories, and lived realities.</p>
<p>Hosted at Chats Palace for a month-long residency throughout August, the exhibition is presented in collaboration with East London Pride, amplifying a shared commitment to visibility, community, and radical joy.<br />
For this exhibition, R.A.G.E LP has partnered with a distinguished group of Black and Brown Queer creatives and collaborators, ensuring that the dialogues explored are grounded in truth, authenticity, and meaningful impact (These creatives being Aleena, Chane, Coco, Moses, Trisha, Sophia). At its core, TAKING UP SPACE is both a declaration and an invitation: a declaration that Black and Brown Queer lives are expansive, complex, and deserving of visibility and an invitation for audiences to witness, reflect, learn and engage. Through striking photographic works, the exhibition explores identity, intimacy, resistance, and self-expression, challenging dominant narratives while carving out new spaces for representation. The residency will transform Chats Palace into a living, breathing cultural hub. Alongside the exhibition, visitors can expect a dynamic programme of events including workshops, community gatherings and shows all designed to deepen dialogue and foster connection.</p>
<p>In collaboration with East London Pride, a series of events will take place throughout August in direct dialogue with the exhibition, creating a wider cultural moment within Chats Palace that celebrates and uplifts Black and Brown Queer communities. These activations will extend the reach of TAKING UP SPACE throughout the venue, fostering visibility, solidarity, and collective celebration.</p>
<p>The exhibition will also feature collaborative works and contributions from Positive East, alongside a range of additional artists and community partners, further enriching the exhibition’s narrative and ensuring a multiplicity of voices and lived experiences are represented. “TAKING UP SPACE is about more than visibility, it’s about ownership,” says Creative Director of East London Pride. “It’s about claiming physical, emotional, and creative space in a world that often tries to minimise or erase. This exhibition is a celebration, but it’s also a necessary act of resistance.”</p>
<p>Whether you come to be moved, challenged, inspired, or simply to witness, TAKING UP SPACE promises an experience that resonates long after you leave the exhibition.</p>

records.title: PRX.LIVE – Live Contemporary Music and World Premieres
records.description: <p>Following the blowout success of our sellout launch party at Folklore, contemporary music magazine PRXLUDES presents a night of music, conversations, and gatherings, celebrating today\'s most cutting-edge composers. Part live gig, part conversation, part social gathering: PRX.LIVE is a platform to gather people, share adventurous music and sounds, and start conversations about art, music, and the world in which we’re creating it. Trailblazing ensemble Standard Issue premiere a new commission by rising-star composer Rebecca Galian Castello, alongside genre-defying works by today\'s most cutting-edge early-career composers and live interviews from PRXLUDES hosts. Hosted by PRXLUDES in partnership with ensemble Standard Issue and producers Stomping Ground. PRX.LIVE and Rebecca Galian Castello\'s commission are generously supported by The Hinrichsen Foundation\'s Multi-Year Partnership and Arts Council England. Programme Rebecca Galian Castello - Peach Fuzz (world premiere, PRXLUDES commission) alongside other works by some of today\'s most exciting composers - full programme to be announced! What is PRXLUDES? PRXLUDES is an online contemporary music magazine, platform, and resource dedicated to the promotion of the most cutting-edge contemporary music of today, with a focus on the work of emerging and early-career composers. The publication specialises in in-depth interviews with composers, ensembles, and organisations promoting the work of emerging artists. https://prxludes.net/</p>\n
